body: I'm surprised this timeout is needed, the algolia client already has timeout logic and should therefore error if not responding soon enough. Are you using a custom client?
in which case is there a response without results?

Hey! Answering to your previous question, yes, this happens when running a custom client. I am working using [searchkit](https://github.com/searchkit/searchkit), but in the end.

I see in the original issue that the reporter uses the typesense adapted, so it might be happening only with custom clients, but I cannot tell 100% sure.

In case the server is down or not responding, the answer may be many things (404, 500, error, nothing...). This is an extra measure to prevent this situations that may return valid a JSON, but not a valid response.
I feel like this is an error in the adapter, and they should throw an error instead. Do you mind making a PR there to fix it instead of handling wrong client behaviour in InstantSearch?
makes sense, can you actually make a similar PR to handle timeouts in the adapters instead of in InstantSearch itself. We can't design our library around differently behaving clients IMO
